html:
Gécamines is the state mining company of the Congo, created on 1 January 1967 when Mobutu nationalised Union Minière du Haut Katanga, the Belgian company that ran the copper mines of Katanga.

In the early 1970s it produced several hundred thousand tonnes of copper a year and supplied most of the state's income, as well as much of the world's cobalt. But under Mobutu its revenue was drained, its equipment decayed, and a mine collapse in 1990 hastened its fall.

By the late 1990s output had nearly stopped. Its mines were later handed to foreign, often Chinese, partners. Its history followed that of Union Minière before it, and its region now leads the world in cobalt, part of the story of conflict minerals.
sum: Gécamines is the state mining company of the Congo, created on 1 January 1967 when Mobutu nationalised Union Minière du Haut Katanga, the Belgian company that ran the copper mines of Katanga.
